# Changed example: validate a book request at the boundary

Export `parseBookRequest(value: unknown)` from your module (TypeScript — but the grader strips types before running, so every rule must hold at RUNTIME).

- Return `{ok: true, request: {title: string, pages?: number}}` or `{ok: false, error: string}`.
- `value` must be a plain object: reject `null`, arrays and non-objects.
- `title`: required string; trim it; after trimming it must be nonempty and at most 80 characters. The stored title is the trimmed one.
- `pages` is OPTIONAL: absent (or `undefined`) is fine and the result then has no `pages` key; when present it must be an integer >= 1 — `0`, `1.5` and `NaN` are all rejected.
- Ignore unknown fields; never throw.

This is the U03 delayed transfer: a book request with a title and an optional integer page count. Type annotations do not validate external JSON — your checks must, because `typeof pages === 'number'` is satisfied by `0`, `1.5` and `NaN` alike.

tests.name: accepts a valid request and trims the title
tests.code: assert.deepEqual(mod.parseBookRequest({ title: '  Dune  ', pages: 412 }), { ok: true, request: { title: 'Dune', pages: 412 } });

tests.name: pages is optional and an absent count leaves no pages key
tests.code:
assert.deepEqual(mod.parseBookRequest({ title: 'Dune' }), { ok: true, request: { title: 'Dune' } });
assert.deepEqual(mod.parseBookRequest({ title: 'Dune', pages: undefined }), { ok: true, request: { title: 'Dune' } });

tests.name: a fractional page count is rejected at runtime
zero and NaN page counts are rejected at runtime
tests.code:
assert.equal(mod.parseBookRequest({ title: 'Dune', pages: 0 }).ok, false);
assert.equal(mod.parseBookRequest({ title: 'Dune', pages: Number.NaN }).ok, false);

tests.name: a page count of 1 is the allowed boundary
tests.code: assert.deepEqual(mod.parseBookRequest({ title: 'Dune', pages: 1 }), { ok: true, request: { title: 'Dune', pages: 1 } });

tests.name: rejects null, arrays and non-string titles
whitespace-only and overlong titles are rejected; exactly 80 characters is allowed

items.wrongBecause: narrows pages with typeof === 'number' only — the annotation-level check: 0, 1.5 and NaN are all numbers to typeof, so invalid page counts cross the boundary; the runtime rule (an integer >= 1) is exactly what type-stripping cannot enforce
